overview: SARS collects taxes that fund government services. Every person who earns income above certain thresholds must register as a taxpayer and submit annual tax returns. SARS also handles VAT registration, customs, transfer duty, and tax clearance certificates. The current tax year runs from 1 March 2024 to 28 February 2025.

who_must_register: Any person earning above R95,750 per year from a single employer
Anyone earning income from more than one source
Anyone with a provisional tax obligation
Anyone earning rental income, freelance income, or investment income
Anyone who has capital gains exceeding the annual exclusion of R40,000
Directors of companies or members of close corporations

tax_brackets_2024_2025.rate: R42,678 + 26% of the amount above R237,100
R77,362 + 31% of the amount above R370,500
R121,475 + 36% of the amount above R512,800
R179,147 + 39% of the amount above R673,000
R251,258 + 41% of the amount above R857,900
R644,489 + 45% of the amount above R1,817,000

tax_rebates_2024_2025.primary_rebate: R17,235 — applies to all individual taxpayers
tax_rebates_2024_2025.secondary_rebate: R9,444 — applies to taxpayers aged 65 and older (in addition to primary rebate)
tax_rebates_2024_2025.tertiary_rebate: R3,145 — applies to taxpayers aged 75 and older (in addition to primary and secondary rebates)

how_to_register: Visit www.sarsefiling.co.za and create an eFiling account
Or visit your nearest SARS branch with your ID and proof of address
You will receive a tax reference number — KEEP THIS SAFE, you will need it forever
You can also register via the SARS MobiApp on your smartphone
efiling_step_by_step: Step 1: Go to www.sarsefiling.co.za and register for an account (you need your ID number, contact details, and a valid email address)
Step 2: Complete the registration wizard — SARS will verify your identity and send a confirmation
Step 3: Log in and navigate to 'Returns' → 'Income Tax' → 'Income Tax Return (ITR12)'
Step 4: Your IRP5 data from your employer should be auto-imported — if not, request the return and SARS will attempt to populate it
Step 5: Review all pre-populated fields carefully — check salary, tax deducted, medical aid contributions, and retirement fund contributions against your IRP5 certificate
Step 6: Add any additional income not pre-populated (rental income, freelance income, foreign income, interest above exempt amount)
Step 7: Claim any allowable deductions (travel allowance, home office, additional medical expenses, donations to approved PBOs)
Step 8: Submit the return — SARS will issue an assessment (ITA34) immediately showing whether you owe tax or are due a refund
Step 9: Track your refund status on eFiling under 'Returns' → 'Tax Status' or call 0800 00 7277

auto_assessment.what_it_is: SARS now auto-assesses many salaried taxpayers using employer and third-party data. If SARS has sufficient information, they will issue an auto-assessment without you needing to file a return.
how_it_works: SARS sends you an SMS or email notifying you of the auto-assessment, typically from early July
Log in to eFiling or SARS MobiApp to view your assessment
If you AGREE with the assessment, you do not need to do anything — it is accepted automatically after the deadline
If you DISAGREE (e.g., you have additional income, deductions, or corrections), you must file a manual return BEFORE the deadline
You can also edit and re-submit even after accepting an auto-assessment, as long as it is before the deadline
auto_assessment.important_note: Do NOT ignore your auto-assessment. Even if you agree, check it carefully. If SARS has incorrect data (e.g., missing deductions), you may be paying more tax than necessary.

tax_season_dates.overview: SARS announces exact dates each year, but the typical schedule is as follows:
tax_season_dates.auto_assessment_notification: From 1 July — SARS begins issuing auto-assessments via SMS/email
tax_season_dates.non_provisional_efiling: 1 July – 23 October — deadline for salaried individuals filing via eFiling or SARS MobiApp
tax_season_dates.non_provisional_branch: 1 July – 23 October — deadline if filing at a SARS branch (by appointment only)
tax_season_dates.provisional_taxpayers: 1 July – 31 January of the following year — extended deadline for provisional taxpayers filing via eFiling
tax_season_dates.note: Always check the SARS website for confirmed dates as they may shift slightly each year

required_documents.overview: Gather all these documents BEFORE you start filing your return:
documents: IRP5/IT3(a) certificate from your employer — this shows your annual salary, tax deducted, and benefits. Contact HR if you have not received it by June
Medical aid tax certificate (from your medical aid scheme) — needed to claim medical tax credits
Retirement annuity (RA) certificate — from your RA fund provider, showing contributions for the year
IT3(b) certificate — from your bank or investment provider, showing interest, dividends, and capital gains
Bank statements — especially if you earned interest income above the exempt amount (R23,800 under 65, R34,500 for 65+)
Logbook for travel allowance — a detailed daily logbook showing business vs. personal kilometres (required by SARS if claiming travel deduction)
Proof of rental income and expenses — lease agreements, bank statements, receipts for repairs and maintenance
Home office expenses documentation — proof of dedicated room used exclusively for work, municipal bills, lease or bond statements
Donation receipts — Section 18A certificates from approved public benefit organisations (PBOs)
Foreign income documentation — if you earned income outside South Africa, including foreign tax certificates

filing_your_tax_return.when: Tax season typically runs from 1 July to 23 October for non-provisional taxpayers and until 31 January for provisional taxpayers (dates announced by SARS annually)
how: Log in to SARS eFiling (www.sarsefiling.co.za) or the SARS MobiApp
Your employer's IRP5 certificate should be pre-populated
Check that the amounts match your payslips and IRP5 certificate
Add any additional income (freelance, rental, investments, foreign income)
Claim allowable deductions (medical aid contributions, retirement fund contributions, travel allowance, home office, donations)
SARS will issue an assessment (ITA34) — either you owe SARS or SARS owes you a refund
first_time_tips: Keep all your payslips — they are your proof if SARS questions anything
Your IRP5 certificate comes from your employer — ask HR for it
If you earned below the threshold and had tax deducted, you MAY get a refund
Medical aid tax credits are automatic if your employer reported them correctly
You can claim for home office expenses ONLY if you have a dedicated room used exclusively for work
Keep ALL supporting documents for at least 5 years — SARS can audit up to 5 years back (longer if fraud is suspected)
If you are unsure about anything, rather file and include everything — SARS will query if needed

travel_allowance.description: If you receive a travel allowance from your employer and use your own vehicle for business travel, you may deduct actual business travel expenses.
requirements: You MUST keep a detailed logbook — record every trip (date, destination, purpose, opening km, closing km, business or personal)
SARS publishes an annual table of deemed costs (fixed cost based on vehicle value + fuel cost per km + maintenance cost per km)
Without a logbook, SARS will only allow 20% of your travel allowance as a deduction (the rest is taxed)
The SARS rate tables are based on the value of the vehicle — higher value vehicles get a higher fixed cost allowance

home_office.description: You may claim home office expenses if you work from home, but the requirements are strict.
requirements: You must have a dedicated room used EXCLUSIVELY for work — a corner of the lounge does NOT qualify
If you earn a salary (regular income earner), you must spend more than 50% of your working time in your home office
If you earn commission income (more than 50% of total pay), the requirements are slightly less strict
Claimable expenses: proportionate share of rent or bond interest, electricity, rates, cleaning, repairs to the office area
The proportion is calculated as office area divided by total area of the home

retirement_contributions.description: Contributions to pension funds, provident funds, and retirement annuity (RA) funds are tax-deductible.
limits: You may deduct the LESSER of 27.5% of your remuneration or 27.5% of your taxable income
The maximum annual deduction is R350,000
Any contributions above the limit are carried forward to future years
This includes contributions made by your employer on your behalf

medical_aid_credits.description: You receive tax credits (not deductions) for medical aid contributions.
credits_2024_2025: Main member + one dependant: R728 per month
Each additional dependant: R246 per month
Additional medical expenses exceeding 7.5% of taxable income can be claimed as a deduction (for under 65s)

donations.description: Donations to approved public benefit organisations (PBOs) with Section 18A status are deductible up to 10% of taxable income.

common_problems: Employer did not submit IRP5 — contact your employer immediately, then report to SARS if they refuse
Assessment shows you owe money you don't have — apply for a payment arrangement at SARS (see payment_arrangements section)
Received assessment for tax you don't owe — dispute the assessment within 30 business days on eFiling
eFiling not working — clear your browser cache, try a different browser, or visit a SARS branch
Outstanding tax returns from previous years — file them all, starting with the oldest year
Auto-assessment is incorrect — file a manual return before the deadline to override it
Refund delayed — check eFiling for verification requests, SARS may need supporting documents
Tax reference number lost — call 0800 00 7277 or visit a branch with your ID to recover it

who_must_pay: Anyone who earns income NOT subject to PAYE (employees' tax), such as:
Director's remuneration from a company where PAYE is not deducted
Investment income exceeding the interest exemption and not subject to withholding tax

payment_schedule.due_date: End of August (6 months into the tax year)
payment_schedule.amount: Estimated tax for the full year, based on projected taxable income — pay at least half

payment_schedule.due_date: End of February (end of the tax year)
payment_schedule.amount: Remaining estimated tax based on actual or revised projected income, minus the first payment
Voluntary payment to avoid interest if your estimate was too low. Only available to taxpayers with a February year-end

provisional_tax.penalties_for_underestimation: If your estimate of taxable income in the second period is less than 80% of actual taxable income (or less than 90% for taxable income exceeding R1 million), SARS may charge an underestimation penalty of up to 20% of the underpaid amount.
provisional_tax.tip: Rather overestimate than underestimate — you can claim any overpayment back as a refund when you file your annual return.

transfer_duty.what_it_is: Transfer duty is a tax payable on the acquisition of property (land and buildings) in South Africa. It is payable by the buyer.

rates_2024_2025.rate: R12,375 + 6% of the value above R1,512,500
R48,675 + 8% of the value above R2,117,500
R97,075 + 11% of the value above R2,722,500
R1,128,600 + 13% of the value above R12,100,000

important_notes: Transfer duty must be paid within 6 months of acquisition, or interest is charged
If the seller is a VAT vendor and the property is sold as part of a going concern, VAT applies instead of transfer duty
No transfer duty is payable if VAT is charged on the transaction
First-time homebuyers buying property up to R1,100,000 pay zero transfer duty

refund_timeline.normal_processing: If your tax affairs are fully compliant (all returns submitted, no outstanding debt, banking details confirmed), refunds are typically paid within 3 to 7 business days after assessment.
possible_delays: SARS verification/audit — SARS may select your return for verification and request supporting documents. This can delay your refund by several weeks.
Incorrect or unconfirmed banking details — log in to eFiling and confirm your banking details are correct and verified
Outstanding returns from previous years — all outstanding returns must be filed before a refund is released
Outstanding tax debt — SARS will offset your refund against any tax debt you owe
Employer IRP5 not submitted — if your employer has not submitted their reconciliation, your refund may be held
refund_timeline.how_to_check: Log in to eFiling → Returns → Tax Status, or call 0800 00 7277 for refund status

verification_and_audit.what_it_is: SARS may select your return for verification or audit to confirm the accuracy of information submitted. This is a routine process and does not mean you did anything wrong.
process: SARS will notify you via eFiling, SMS, or email that your return has been selected for verification
You will be told which supporting documents are required (e.g., IRP5, logbook, medical certificates, bank statements)
You have 21 business days from the date of the request to submit the required documents via eFiling
Upload documents on eFiling under 'Returns' → 'Supporting Documents'
SARS will review the documents and issue a revised assessment or confirm the original assessment
if_you_disagree: If you disagree with the revised assessment after verification, you may file a Notice of Objection within 30 business days
File the objection on eFiling under 'Disputes' → 'Notice of Objection'
SARS must respond to your objection — if they disallow it, you can appeal within 30 business days
If the appeal is unsuccessful, you may apply for Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) or approach the Tax Court
tips: Respond within 21 days — if you miss the deadline, SARS may issue an additional assessment
Upload clear, legible copies of all requested documents
If you need more time, request an extension on eFiling before the deadline expires
Keep copies of everything you submit

payment_arrangements.what_it_is: If you owe SARS and cannot pay the full amount, you may apply for a payment arrangement (installment plan).
how_to_apply: Log in to eFiling → Payments → Payment Plan Request
Or call SARS on 0800 00 7277 to discuss your situation
Or visit a SARS branch with your ID and supporting documents showing your financial situation
You will need to propose a realistic payment schedule that SARS must approve
important_notes: Interest is charged on the outstanding balance at the prescribed rate (repo rate + 4%)
You must make payments on time — if you default on the arrangement, SARS may cancel it and pursue collection
A payment arrangement does NOT stop interest from accruing, but it prevents SARS from taking immediate enforcement action
SARS may require proof of your financial situation (bank statements, income proof, list of expenses)

tax_clearance_certificate.what_it_is: A Tax Compliance Certificate (TCC) confirms that your tax affairs are in order. Required for government tenders, certain visa applications, foreign investment allowances, and large financial transactions.
how_to_get: Step 1: Log in to SARS eFiling
Step 2: Navigate to 'Tax Compliance Status' → 'Apply for TCC'
Step 3: Select the type of TCC you need (Good Standing, Tender, Foreign Investment Allowance, or Emigration)
Step 4: Submit the application — SARS will verify your compliance status
Step 5: If compliant, a TCC PIN is generated — share this PIN with the party who requires it (e.g., government department, bank)
Step 6: The requirer verifies your TCC using the PIN on the SARS website
tax_clearance_certificate.validity: A TCC is valid for 12 months from the date of issue.
requirements: All tax returns must be up to date (no outstanding returns)
Any tax debt must be settled or under an approved payment arrangement
Your eFiling profile must have confirmed and verified banking details
If there are issues, SARS will tell you what needs to be resolved first

vat_registration.who_must_register: Any business (including sole proprietors) with taxable supplies exceeding R1 million in any 12-month period MUST register for VAT.
vat_registration.voluntary_registration: Businesses with taxable supplies exceeding R50,000 in a 12-month period may register voluntarily. This can be beneficial if your clients are VAT-registered businesses.
how_to_register: Apply on SARS eFiling under 'Organisations' → 'Register New'
Provide proof of business activity, bank statements, invoices, lease agreement
SARS may conduct a verification visit to your business premises
Once registered, you must submit VAT returns every 2 months (Category A) or monthly (Category C for larger businesses)
vat_registration.vat_rate: The standard VAT rate in South Africa is 15%.

common_scams.overview: SARS scams are common and becoming more sophisticated. Fraudsters impersonate SARS to steal your personal information or money.
types_of_scams: Phishing emails that look like they come from SARS, asking you to click a link and enter your login details or banking information
SMS messages claiming you are due a refund and asking you to reply with your banking details
Fake eFiling websites that look identical to the real site — always check the URL is www.sarsefiling.co.za
Phone calls from people claiming to be SARS agents demanding immediate payment by EFT or voucher
Emails with attachments claiming to be your tax assessment — these may contain malware
how_to_protect_yourself: SARS will NEVER ask for your banking details, passwords, or PINs via email, SMS, or phone
SARS will NEVER send you a link to update your banking details
SARS will NEVER threaten you with immediate arrest for unpaid tax
Always access eFiling by typing www.sarsefiling.co.za directly in your browser — never click links in emails
If in doubt, call SARS directly on 0800 00 7277 to verify any communication
Report suspected scams to SARS at 0800 00 2870 (fraud hotline)

late_submission.individuals: R250 per month for each month the return is outstanding, up to a maximum of 35 months (R8,750 total)
late_submission.companies_and_trusts: Penalty ranges from R250 to R16,000 per month depending on the entity's assessed loss or taxable income, up to 35 months

understatement_penalty.description: If SARS finds that you understated your taxable income or overstated deductions, an understatement penalty applies based on the behaviour:
rates: Substantial understatement (no reasonable grounds): 10% of the shortfall
Reasonable care not taken: 25% of the shortfall
No reasonable grounds for tax position: 50% of the shortfall
Intentional tax evasion: 150% of the shortfall
Repeat offender (intentional or gross negligence + obstructive): 200% of the shortfall

penalties.non_registration: Failure to register as a taxpayer when required: a fine of up to R16,000 or imprisonment of up to 24 months.
penalties.late_payment: Interest is charged on late payment of tax at the prescribed rate (currently repo rate + 4%). A 10% penalty may also be levied on the late amount.
penalties.criminal_offences: Tax evasion, fraud, and failure to submit returns are criminal offences under the Tax Administration Act. Convictions can result in fines and imprisonment.

sars_offices_ethekwini.name: SARS Durban CBD
sars_offices_ethekwini.address: Kingsmead Office Park, 2 Kingsmead Way, Durban
sars_offices_ethekwini.tip: Book an appointment online before visiting — walk-ins face very long waits

important_contacts.sars_mobiapp: Available on Google Play Store and Apple App Store

escalation.step_1: Use SARS eFiling to dispute an assessment — you have 30 business days from the assessment date
escalation.step_2: If SARS does not resolve your dispute, request Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) through eFiling
escalation.step_3: If ADR fails, appeal to the Tax Court within 30 business days of the ADR outcome
escalation.step_4: Contact the Tax Ombud for complaints about SARS service: 0800 662 837 or www.taxombud.gov.za
escalation.step_5: As a last resort, you may approach the High Court for judicial review of SARS decisions
escalation.legislation: Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011, Income Tax Act 58 of 1962, Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991

your_rights: You have the right to be treated fairly and with respect at any SARS office
You have the right to clear explanations of any tax assessment
You have the right to dispute any assessment within 30 business days
You have the right to a payment arrangement if you cannot pay your tax debt in full
SARS must process refunds within a reasonable time — persistent delays can be reported to the Tax Ombud
You have the right to confidentiality of your tax information
SARS may not attach your primary residence to settle tax debt below R250,000 without a court order
You have the right to be informed of the reasons for any SARS decision affecting you
You have the right to appoint a tax practitioner to act on your behalf
You have the right to request reasons for any delay in processing your return or refund
